q: how much does a gorilla weigh
a: Gorillas are the largest living primates, belonging to the great ape family alongside chimpanzees, orangutans, and bonobos. There are two species: the eastern gorilla (including the critically endangered mountain gorilla) and the western gorilla (including the lowland gorilla), both native to the forests of central Africa. Adult male silverbacks weigh 135-220 kg and stand about 1.7 meters tall, and they are enormously strong — estimates suggest a gorilla can lift roughly 10 times its body weight, far beyond any human, with a bite force around 1,300 PSI. Gorillas are gentle, intelligent herbivores that eat mostly leaves, stems, fruit, and bamboo, and they live in family groups led by a dominant silverback male. They share about 98% of their DNA with humans, use tools, and show complex emotions and communication.
